subject: Trial onboarding & acceptance criteria — next steps and risk owners
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena@datasync.ai>, Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Trial onboarding & acceptance criteria — next steps and risk owners

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and concrete next steps so we have shared alignment for the POC trial window. High-level goal: validate Redwood inference for your batch analytics workload and a small set of low-latency web endpoints.

Summary / success criteria (proposed):
- Throughput: sustain 500 concurrent inference requests with median 95ms token latency for the web routes.
- Accuracy: model responses match your rubric >= 88% on the 200-case prompt set (we'll run automated evals).
- Cost: projected per-1M-token runtime cost under $45 via batching/quantization recommendations.
- Integrations: S3 data pull + API key-based auth in place; end-to-end test run with your sample data.

Proposed trial timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): onboarding, access exchange, and infra checklist (I attached POC-checklist.xlsx).
- Week 1: model onboarding + sample-run (owner: Dev).
- Week 2: evaluation run against 200-case prompt set; automated scoring (owner: Connor + DataSync).
- Week 3: review and decision; collect feedback and go/no-go.

Owners & contacts:
- Connor O'Brien (me): overall trial coordinator, evaluation plan, success criteria.
- Dev Patel: integration lead, sandbox setup, debug owner for infra issues.
- Marissa Cole: commercial point for contract / SLA / procurement escalations.

Known risks & initial mitigations:
- Data access delays (risk): need temporary token/temporary S3 read creds. Mitigation: provide scoped token for dev sandbox; HR/legal to follow for long-term.
- Model mismatch (risk): if model variant differences cause failures in evals. Mitigation: run small compatibility test first; Dev to prototype model shim.
- GPU capacity (operational): potential affect to performance targets in peak windows. Mitigation: Redwood can schedule dedicated capacity for the trial week if needed (we'll confirm after Week 1).

Please reply with any changes to the success criteria or timeline. If that looks good, I'll mark owners and get the onboarding items scheduled (Dev — can you confirm available windows for the sandbox this week?).

Attachments: POC-checklist.xlsx (overview + access steps)

--
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189
From: Lena Park <lena@datasync.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial onboarding & acceptance criteria — next steps and risk owners

Thanks Connor — appreciate the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Acceptance metric: the 88% rubric is fine but we need to confirm how edge-case failure is handled; can we get a breakdown by category (NLP-generalization vs. hallucination-rate) in the Week 2 automated report?

2) Data access: we'll need to route the sample dataset through our S3 with a short-term read token. Security asked if Redwood can support limited-time presigned URLs instead of long-lived keys.

3) Audit logs / compliance: We will need proof of request-level audit logs during the trial (timestamped request IDs + response hashes). Is that available out-of-the-box or do we need to enable a feature?

We can confirm the sample 200-case prompt set by EOD Thursday. Tom and I prefer a Tuesday morning review in Week 3 (US/PST).

On the risks: regarding GPU capacity — if you need to provision dedicated capacity, can you include a rough delta on cost vs hosted? We need to include that in our internal cost model.

Thanks — Lena
Lena Park
Head of ML Ops | DataSync AI
lena@datasync.ai
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena@datasync.ai>, Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial onboarding & acceptance criteria — next steps and risk owners

Great questions — answers inline and next steps.

Lena — acceptance breakdown: yes, we'll produce per-category metrics (generalization vs hallucination). Connor (me) + DataSync team will own the rubric mapping. We'll add a column to the Week 2 report for those buckets.

Data access: presigned URLs work fine. We can accept a 24-72 hour presigned S3 URL for the bulk sample and use scoped temp tokens for API calls. Dev — can you prepare an instruction snippet for presigned ingestion?

Audit logs: Redwood can provide request-level logs for the trial. We'll enable detailed logging and provide a CSV of request_id, timestamp, route, and response_hash. Note: this adds a small storage delta; Marissa, can procurement confirm if DataSync wants logs exported to their bucket or hosted temporarily by Redwood?

GPU capacity & cost delta: rough numbers: hosted burst mode (no dedicated) is +0% base but subject to queue; dedicated trial pool estimated at $6k/week for the capacity profile discussed. I'll have exact numbers by EOD.

Updated timeline / immediate asks:
- Today: Dev to share sandbox availability + presigned ingestion instructions (Dev: please add ETA).
- Thu (EOD): DataSync to confirm 200-case prompt set.
- Next Tue (Week 3): review session.

Escalation path if blockers arise:
- Level 1: Dev Patel (integration/infra).
- Level 2: Marissa Cole (commercial & procurement).
- Level 3: Connor O'Brien / Redwood exec escalation.

Thanks — I'll update the checklist and post the timeline link.

--
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Lena Park <lena@datasync.ai>, Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial onboarding & acceptance criteria — next steps and risk owners

Connor — I'll own the sandbox work. Quick tech notes / potential blockers I expect after reviewing the sample shapes: 

1) Model variant compatibility: your sample payloads include tokenized tokens we haven't validated against the v2-legacy model. Action: I will run a compatibility shim in the sandbox to catch tokenization mismatches. ETA: 48 hours.

2) Presigned ingestion: presigned URLs are fine. I'll add a short instructions doc and a curl example for ingestion to the sandbox. Attachment: integration-instructions.md (text).

3) Dataset sensitivity: there are PHI-ish fields in a subset of the sample. We recommend sanitizing before ingestion — otherwise we can route to a private trial VPC (requires procurement sign-off).

4) GPU availability: not blocking yet, but if evaluation runs overlap peak jobs we may see degraded latency. Workaround: schedule evaluation runs off-peak or request a small dedicated pool for Week 1. Please confirm which you prefer; I'll test with a 10k-sample dry run first.

I'll attach the integration-instructions.md and post the sandbox windows (Thu 10–12, Fri 9–11 PST).

--
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Platform
dev@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-04T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial onboarding & acceptance criteria — next steps and risk owners

Thanks team — all good on our side. A few commercial / ops notes: 

- Logs export: DataSync — we can export the trial audit logs to your S3 bucket; please confirm the bucket name and access window. That avoids extra storage billing on Redwood.
- Procurement: if you choose a dedicated pool for Week 1, we'll draft a one-week commitment addendum; Connor will circulate numbers.
- Weekly sync: Connor, please set up a recurring 30-min stand for Tuesdays at 9am PST starting week after next; invite Dev + Lena + Tom + me.

Escalation contacts for quick resolution: 
- Dev Patel (primary tech) — dev@redwood.com
- Marissa Cole (commercial) — marissa@redwood.com
- Connor O'Brien (exec escalation) — connor@redwood.com

Connor — once you post the updated checklist and the presigned-instruction snippet from Dev, I'll mark this as RAG: Amber (minor risk: dataset sensitivity & possible dedicated pool).

--
